templates.description: One integrity-covered member (skill text, schema annotation, manifest or graph value) is changed after signing; integrity.json and the signature are untouched.
templates.forbidden_boundary: The edited package reaches a ready Run Plan, a lease or execution.
templates.matched_control: The same edit, rebuilt and signed by an operator-pinned key.
templates.title: Signed payload edited, integrity statement left as signed
templates.violated_assumption: The payload bytes are the bytes the publisher's integrity statement describes.

templates.description: The member is changed and integrity.json is recomputed over the edited payload, which any party can do; the publisher's signature is left as it was.
templates.forbidden_boundary: The edited package reaches a ready Run Plan, a lease or execution.
templates.matched_control: The same edit, rebuilt and signed by an operator-pinned key.
templates.title: Signed payload edited, integrity statement recomputed
templates.violated_assumption: The integrity statement is the one the publisher signed.

templates.description: As above, and the signature envelope's `digest` field is rewritten to the new statement, so only the Ed25519 signature bytes still belong to the old content.
templates.forbidden_boundary: The edited package reaches a ready Run Plan, a lease or execution.
templates.matched_control: The same edit, rebuilt and signed by an operator-pinned key.
templates.title: Signed payload edited, statement and signed digest rewritten
templates.violated_assumption: The Ed25519 signature verifies over the integrity statement.

templates.description: A new data member is inserted into the signed archive; the integrity statement does not list it.
templates.forbidden_boundary: The extended package reaches a ready Run Plan, a lease or execution.
templates.matched_control: The same member added, rebuilt and signed by an operator-pinned key.
templates.title: Member added after signing
templates.violated_assumption: The archive holds exactly the members the integrity statement covers.

templates.description: One integrity-covered member is removed from the signed archive.
templates.forbidden_boundary: The truncated package reaches a ready Run Plan, a lease or execution.
templates.matched_control: The unmodified signed artifact.
templates.title: Signed member deleted
templates.violated_assumption: Every member the integrity statement covers is present.

templates.description: A second entry with an authoritative member's name and different content is added. General-purpose ZIP readers accept this (Python's keeps the last one).
templates.forbidden_boundary: The ambiguous package reaches a ready Run Plan, a lease or execution.
templates.matched_control: The unmodified signed artifact.
templates.title: Ambiguous archive: duplicate member names
templates.violated_assumption: Each member name denotes exactly one byte sequence.

templates.description: The signed members are kept, but the ZIP container carries a prefix, suffix, comment, extra field, data descriptor, compression, an executable or symlink mode, or a directory entry. Most general-purpose ZIP readers accept these.
templates.forbidden_boundary: The non-canonical package reaches a ready Run Plan, a lease or execution.
templates.matched_control: The unmodified signed artifact.
templates.title: Non-canonical container layout
templates.violated_assumption: The artifact is one canonical, data-only ZIP_STORED container.

templates.description: A member with a traversal, absolute, reserved, executable, credential-like or case-colliding name — signed by an operator-pinned key, so signature and trust hold.
templates.forbidden_boundary: The package reaches a ready Run Plan, a lease or execution.
templates.matched_control: The same content under a safe relative name, signed by the same pinned key.
templates.title: Unsafe or executable member name in a trusted package
templates.violated_assumption: Package members are portable, data-only relative names.

templates.description: A JSON member with a duplicated key (different values), a non-JSON NaN literal, or a text member that is not UTF-8 or contains NUL — signed by an operator-pinned key. Python's own json module accepts duplicate keys (last wins) and NaN.
templates.forbidden_boundary: The package reaches a ready Run Plan, a lease or execution.
templates.matched_control: The same member with one unambiguous value, signed by the same pinned key.
templates.title: Ambiguous or invalid document in a trusted package
templates.violated_assumption: Every package document has exactly one unambiguous meaning.

templates.description: The package is structurally valid and its Ed25519 signature verifies, but the signing key is not in the operator's trust store (or the claimed publisher is pinned to a different key).
templates.forbidden_boundary: The package reaches a ready Run Plan, a lease or execution.
templates.matched_control: The same bytes after the signer is pinned (by the operator, or by the page's Trust action).
templates.title: Valid signature from a key the host has not pinned
templates.violated_assumption: Execution requires an operator-pinned publisher key, not merely a valid signature.

templates.description: The signing key is pinned, but the pin is bound to another publisher id or to another package id prefix, which the trust store reports as a mismatch (an impersonation signal).
templates.forbidden_boundary: The package reaches a ready Run Plan, a lease or execution.
templates.matched_control: The same key pinned for the package's own publisher id and package scope.
templates.title: Signer pinned, but for a different publisher or package
templates.violated_assumption: A pin authorizes exactly the publisher and package scope it names.

templates.description: The payload and integrity statement are valid, but the artifact carries no publisher signature at all, so no publisher identity exists to trust.
templates.forbidden_boundary: The package reaches a ready Run Plan, a lease or execution.
templates.matched_control: The same payload signed by an operator-pinned key.
templates.title: Unsigned package
templates.violated_assumption: Only a signed package can be attributed to a publisher the host trusts.

templates.description: The person denies one permission the package marks required; every other decision, approval, requirement and the trust state are unchanged.
templates.forbidden_boundary: A Run Plan, lease or execution exists although a required permission is denied.
templates.matched_control: Every permission granted for the session.
templates.title: Required permission denied
templates.violated_assumption: A run proceeds only with every required permission granted.

templates.description: Literature Review declares its model permission optional (it can replay fixtures); a model-backed run needs it anyway. The person denies it.
templates.forbidden_boundary: A Run Plan, lease or execution exists without the model permission.
templates.matched_control: The model permission granted.
templates.title: Model-run permission denied
templates.violated_assumption: A model-backed run requires the package's model permission even when the package calls it optional.

templates.description: Every permission is granted, but one declared, host-bound tool is not explicitly approved.
templates.forbidden_boundary: A Run Plan, lease or execution exists although a bound tool is unapproved.
templates.matched_control: Every tool approved.
templates.title: Tool approval withheld
templates.violated_assumption: A granted permission is not an approval: every tool needs its own.

templates.description: The person grants a permission 'once'; the package's graph would consume that kind of authority more than once.
templates.forbidden_boundary: The once-granted authority is exercised more than once.
templates.matched_control: The same permission granted for the session.
templates.title: One-time grant the workflow would use repeatedly
templates.violated_assumption: A once-only grant is used at most once; it is never silently widened to the session.

templates.description: A person's document is attached to (or named by) a run whose selected-file permission is denied. The permission is optional in the package, so the plan itself is legal.
templates.forbidden_boundary: The document is parsed, or a paper-reader call is dispatched to the host.
templates.matched_control: The selected-file permission granted with the document attached.
templates.title: Selected document without the file permission
templates.violated_assumption: Reading a selected file requires the file permission, separately from selecting it.

templates.description: The task names a document id for a run whose selected-file permission is denied and to which no file is attached. Nothing at start refers to a file, so the read itself is the decision point.
templates.forbidden_boundary: The document is parsed, or a paper-reader call is dispatched to the host.
templates.matched_control: The selected-file permission granted with the document attached.
templates.title: Document named by the task without the file permission
templates.violated_assumption: Reading a selected file requires the file permission at the moment of the read.

templates.description: The caller prepares a plan against a receipt that is not this session's current one, or authorizes while echoing a different package's digest.
templates.forbidden_boundary: A Run Plan, lease or execution is created from the mismatched consent.
templates.matched_control: The same flow echoing this session's own receipt and digest.
templates.title: Consent bound to the wrong session, receipt or bytes
templates.violated_assumption: A receipt is bound to the exact session and bytes it was issued for and cannot be replayed.

templates.description: The authorization receipt is valid now but expires before the host's run deadline.
templates.forbidden_boundary: A lease is issued or execution starts under consent that ends mid-run.
templates.matched_control: Consent that outlasts the whole run deadline.
templates.title: Consent that expires before the run could finish
templates.violated_assumption: A run starts only under consent that outlasts it.

templates.description: The host's descriptor for the selected model reports fewer context tokens than the package's model requirements declare.
templates.forbidden_boundary: A completion is dispatched to the model that does not meet the requirement.
templates.matched_control: The same model reporting a sufficient context window (at the boundary: the smallest context the calibrated calls reserve).
templates.title: Selected model's context window below the package requirement
templates.violated_assumption: The bound model satisfies every declared hard requirement.

templates.description: The selected model is declared not to support reasoning, or its catalog row is silent about it, while every package task requires it.
templates.forbidden_boundary: A completion is dispatched to the model that does not (verifiably) meet the requirement.
templates.matched_control: The same model declaring the capability.
templates.title: Selected model lacks (or does not confirm) a required capability
templates.violated_assumption: A capability the host cannot confirm is not assumed.

templates.description: The model the person selects is listed but not routable, not permitted to the plugin, or retired.
templates.forbidden_boundary: A completion is dispatched for a model the host does not offer.
templates.matched_control: The same model offered by the host.
templates.title: Selected model not usable on this host
templates.violated_assumption: A plan binds only a model the host can actually invoke for this plugin.

templates.description: Every permission and approval is granted, but the host offers no enabled implementation of one declared tool (or of any).
templates.forbidden_boundary: The tool's (absent or disabled) implementation executes.
templates.matched_control: Every declared tool bound to its enabled built-in implementation.
templates.title: Declared tool without a usable host implementation
templates.violated_assumption: Every declared tool is bound to an enabled host implementation before anything runs.

templates.description: The host's implementation of a declared tool differs from the package's signed declaration: schema digests, capability name, side effects, permission class, destination, method, or more than one candidate.
templates.forbidden_boundary: The mismatched implementation executes.
templates.matched_control: The tool's exact built-in implementation.
templates.title: Host tool implementation does not match the declared contract
templates.violated_assumption: The bound implementation speaks exactly the contract the package declared.

templates.description: The OpenClaw host reports a release other than the one the plugin's token accounting was verified on, with the default policy that requires a verified host.
templates.forbidden_boundary: Package instructions start executing on the unverified host.
templates.matched_control: The verified OpenClaw release (2026.9.5).
templates.title: Host runtime release the accounting was not verified against
templates.violated_assumption: Execution runs only on the host release whose accounting the contract was verified against.

templates.description: A trusted, validly signed package declares a minimum runtime version above the installed agentpkg.
templates.forbidden_boundary: The package reaches a ready Run Plan, a lease or execution.
templates.matched_control: The same trusted package declaring the installed minimum version.
templates.title: Package requires a newer runtime than the host has
templates.violated_assumption: A package runs only on a runtime that meets its declared minimum version.

templates.description: A real, signed and trusted artifact whose entrypoint is a profile other than workflow.v0.
templates.forbidden_boundary: The package reaches a ready Run Plan, a lease or execution.
templates.matched_control: The current workflow.v0 artifact of the same package.
templates.title: Package for an execution profile this host does not install
templates.violated_assumption: A package executes only under an installed execution profile.

templates.description: After a ready plan exists, the person authorizes again (identically, or withdrawing a permission or an approval), and then presses Run on the earlier plan.
templates.forbidden_boundary: The superseded plan's run starts executing.
templates.matched_control: The same plan, started with no intervening authorization.
templates.title: Consent changed after the plan was frozen
templates.violated_assumption: A plan is bound to the one receipt it was prepared under; newer consent supersedes it.

templates.description: After a ready plan exists, the operator removes or re-scopes the publisher's pin, so the signer is no longer trusted for this package.
templates.forbidden_boundary: The run starts executing after trust was withdrawn.
templates.matched_control: An unrelated pin added after the plan; this publisher remains trusted.
templates.title: Publisher trust withdrawn after the plan was frozen
templates.violated_assumption: Trust is re-checked at start, not inherited from preparation time.

templates.description: After a ready plan exists, the host stops offering the bound model (removed, unroutable, retired, or no longer permitted), where OpenClaw would otherwise fall back silently to its default model or refuse.
templates.forbidden_boundary: Any completion is dispatched under the plan after its model stopped being offered.
templates.matched_control: The same kind of host change applied to a model the plan does not use.
templates.title: Bound model withdrawn or substituted after the plan was frozen
templates.violated_assumption: Every completion is made on the plan's model, or not at all; no silent substitution.

templates.description: After a ready plan exists, the host's implementation of one approved tool is disabled, retargeted, re-bounded, re-versioned or removed.
templates.forbidden_boundary: The tool executes through the changed (or no longer approved) implementation.
templates.matched_control: The same binding relabelled after the plan (labels are not part of its identity).
templates.title: Approved tool implementation changed after the plan was frozen
templates.violated_assumption: A plan binds one exact implementation (by digest); a different one is never substituted.

templates.description: After a ready plan exists, the control plane's private snapshot of the package is rewritten in place (another valid release, a flipped byte, or a truncation).
templates.forbidden_boundary: Package instructions start executing from the changed bytes.
templates.matched_control: The same plan with the snapshot untouched.
templates.title: Frozen package snapshot changed after the plan
templates.violated_assumption: The bytes that run are byte-for-byte the bytes that were verified and authorized.

templates.description: The one-time lease the host opened for the runner is rewritten in place after the lease was issued and before the runner reads it.
templates.forbidden_boundary: Package instructions start executing from the changed bytes.
templates.matched_control: The same run with the lease untouched.
templates.title: Leased package bytes changed before the runner read them
templates.violated_assumption: The runner executes only the bytes the plan names (archive hash, digest, signer).

templates.description: Run names a superseded plan, a wrong plan hash, or another session's plan.
templates.forbidden_boundary: Package instructions start executing although the requested plan is not the session's plan.
templates.matched_control: Run naming the session's current plan.
templates.title: Run started against a plan other than the session's current one
templates.violated_assumption: Run acts only on the exact plan (id and hash) the caller read and the session holds.

templates.description: The host's model stack answers one call with a different model (OpenClaw's documented fallback to the agent default, a remote model, or a provider swap) and reports it.
templates.forbidden_boundary: The substituted model's answer enters committed workflow state or the published result.
templates.matched_control: The bound model answers, reporting a different provider snapshot name.
templates.title: Model call answered by a model other than the bound one
templates.violated_assumption: Nothing a model the person did not choose wrote is used.

templates.description: A trusted (pinned, validly signed) package's graph adds an argument to a tool call — a URL, endpoint, header, method, extra query parameter or file path — beside the ones the tool declares.
templates.forbidden_boundary: The host broker serves a call carrying the undeclared argument, a request leaves with a destination, field or parameter the host did not fix, or a canary file is opened.
templates.matched_control: The same trusted package without the extra argument.
templates.title: Tool call carrying arguments that would shape the request
templates.violated_assumption: A package chooses argument values within its declared schema, never where or how a request is sent.

templates.description: A model output or a trusted package's graph names, for the PDF reader, a capability id the run was not given, a non-capability token, an absolute or relative path to a canary file, or a file:// URL.
templates.forbidden_boundary: A canary file is opened, or bytes other than the attached document reach the parser.
templates.matched_control: The run reading only its attached document.
templates.title: File read naming something other than a selected-file capability
templates.violated_assumption: Only the files the person selected and attached to this run are readable, by opaque id.

templates.description: A model answer gives the PDF reader an absolute or relative path to a canary file instead of a document id. The answer's own schema constrains document ids, so it is refused before any read is attempted.
templates.forbidden_boundary: A canary file is opened, or bytes other than the attached document reach the parser.
templates.matched_control: The run reading only its attached document.
templates.primary_guard: output schema (document id pattern), then the broker's capability check
templates.title: Model answer naming a file path for the reader
templates.violated_assumption: Only the files the person selected and attached to this run are readable, by opaque id.

templates.description: A trusted package's graph calls an undeclared tool or model task, lets a role use a tool it does not list, runs effects on the coordinator, reads or writes state outside a worker's declared view, or exports a file under a name the package format reserves for the host. Static workflow validation is not removed by any profile (it is what makes a graph executable); the runtime confinement removed by -Mediation is its backstop.
templates.forbidden_boundary: The package reaches a ready Run Plan, a lease or execution.
templates.matched_control: The same trusted package without the out-of-bounds node.
templates.title: Graph reaching beyond its declared capabilities
templates.violated_assumption: A graph can only do what its own declarations (tools, tasks, roles, state views) allow.

templates.description: A trusted package declares an export whose name collides (case-insensitively) with run.json, the record the execution host writes beside the package's artifacts. The package format itself does not reserve this name; the execution host does.
templates.forbidden_boundary: A package-written file appears among the run's artifacts under a host-reserved name.
templates.matched_control: The same export under a non-reserved name.
templates.title: Export named like the execution host's run record
templates.violated_assumption: A package writes only its own declared exports, never a host-owned file.

templates.description: A trusted package re-declares a remote tool at another domain (and grants itself that domain consistently), hoping the host will send the tool's data there — or will send it to its usual service under the new, differently-scoped permission.
templates.forbidden_boundary: Tool data is sent to a destination outside the permission resources the person granted.
templates.matched_control: The same trusted package with its original declarations.
templates.title: Package declares a tool destination the host binding does not serve
templates.violated_assumption: A package's declared endpoint bounds a binding; it never grants or redirects one.

templates.description: The approved binding's hostname resolves (for example after DNS rebinding) to a loopback, private, link-local/metadata, CGNAT or IPv4-mapped address.
templates.forbidden_boundary: A connection is attempted to a non-public address.
templates.matched_control: The same hostname resolving to a public address.
templates.title: Approved tool host resolves to a non-public address
templates.violated_assumption: Tool traffic reaches only publicly routable destinations.

templates.description: One model call's answer (well-formed JSON) violates the node's declared output schema at one location: a missing required field, an undeclared property, a wrong type, a value outside an enum, a bound or a pattern, or an array outside its size limits. Sites are enumerated from the package's own schemas, sampled per model task across operators (the preset's parametric budget per task), and each is checked against the router's schema.
templates.forbidden_boundary: The node that asked for the answer commits it to workflow state.
templates.matched_control: The same answer changed at a free-text or free-enum location the schema accepts.
templates.title: Model answer that breaks its declared output schema
templates.violated_assumption: A model answer is used only if it satisfies the output schema its node declares.

templates.description: One model call returns no text, prose, a truncated or trailing-comma document, a Python literal, or a fenced truncated document.
templates.forbidden_boundary: The node that asked for the answer commits anything.
templates.matched_control: The same valid JSON inside a markdown fence or surrounded by prose (forms the router reads).
templates.primary_guard: router parse (not removable: an unparsed answer has no value)
templates.title: Model answer that is not one JSON document
templates.violated_assumption: An answer that is not one parseable JSON document is refused, never repaired or retried.

templates.description: One model call's text is a complete, schema-valid document, but the host reports the turn as stopped at the output limit, failed (error, refusal, filter), aborted, or ended for a tool call.
templates.forbidden_boundary: The node that asked for the answer commits it.
templates.matched_control: The same answer with the turn reported finished, or with no stop reason reported.
templates.title: Model turn the provider did not finish
templates.violated_assumption: Only a finished turn's answer is used; an unfinished one is classified, not parsed.

templates.description: A schema-valid extraction answer quotes text that is not in the document page or abstract it cites, attributes the evidence to another paper, cites a page the document does not have, or mislabels abstract evidence as full-text.
templates.forbidden_boundary: The evidence map commits the unsupported evidence to workflow state.
templates.matched_control: A shortened verbatim quote, or a paraphrased free-text field with the quote unchanged.
templates.title: Extracted evidence that its source does not support
templates.violated_assumption: Every evidence item quotes its own paper's source verbatim, at the location it names (the package's check-document / check-abstract relations).

templates.description: A schema-valid verification answer adds a bibliography entry, claim citation or evidence-table row that the run's resolved citations and extracted evidence do not support, or attributes a direct quote to another paper.
templates.forbidden_boundary: The published review contains the unsupported citation, quote or row.
templates.matched_control: The answer reworded where no relation applies (a rewritten table row the package re-materializes from state, a paraphrased synthesis claim, renumbered references).
templates.title: Review that cites, quotes or tabulates what its evidence does not support
templates.violated_assumption: The published review cites only resolved papers and existing evidence, and every direct quote is its own paper's (the package's lookups, check-direct-source and validate-output).

templates.description: The resolver's answer for one selected paper violates the tool's declared output schema, or is not a JSON response.
templates.forbidden_boundary: The citations map commits the bad resolution to workflow state.
templates.matched_control: A resolver answer with an informational extra field, or a different valid venue string.
templates.title: Citation Resolver answer that breaks the tool's output contract
templates.violated_assumption: A tool answer is used only if it is JSON and satisfies the tool's declared output schema.

templates.description: The resolver's schema-valid answer for one selected paper names a different paper of the corpus, a DOI that is not the requested one, or no match while claiming resolution.
templates.forbidden_boundary: The citations map commits the wrong resolution to workflow state.
templates.matched_control: A resolver answer with an informational extra field, or a different valid venue string.
templates.title: Citation Resolver answer that resolves the wrong paper
templates.violated_assumption: A resolution is used only for the paper that was asked about (the package's check-identity relation).

templates.description: Crossref's answer to one planned query is mislabelled, not JSON, not an ok work list, or larger than the binding allows.
templates.forbidden_boundary: The search map commits a result built from the bad answer.
templates.matched_control: Crossref answers carrying fields the adapter does not read.
templates.title: Scholarly-search answer that is not a usable Crossref work list
templates.violated_assumption: A tool answer is used only if it is a JSON response of the declared type and size that the host adapter can read as the declared result.

templates.description: The host's PDF text extraction for the selected document returns pages numbered from 0, no pages, an undeclared source label, or non-text page content.
templates.forbidden_boundary: The screening map commits a result built from the bad answer.
templates.matched_control: The reader's answer with an informational extra field the schema allows.
templates.title: PDF reader answer that breaks the tool's output schema
templates.violated_assumption: A tool answer is used only if it satisfies the tool's declared output schema.

templates.description: The operator's per-run token budget is set below what the workflow reserves; every other setting is the benign one.
templates.forbidden_boundary: Used plus reserved tokens exceed the budget at any point of the run.
templates.matched_control: A budget of 125% of the calibrated peak.
templates.title: Run needs more tokens than the host's budget
templates.violated_assumption: Reserved plus used tokens never exceed the effective budget; a call that would is refused before it is dispatched.

templates.description: A trusted package declares one worker a token budget smaller than the reservation its first model call needs.
templates.forbidden_boundary: The worker's call is dispatched (or its node commits) beyond its declared budget.
templates.matched_control: The worker's budget set exactly to that reservation.
templates.title: Worker call larger than the worker's declared token budget
templates.violated_assumption: A worker never reserves more tokens than its own declared budget.

templates.description: The host's per-run remote-call budget, or one worker role's package-declared per-instance remote-call budget, is below what the workflow (or one instance) makes.
templates.forbidden_boundary: More remote requests leave than the budget allows.
templates.matched_control: A budget exactly equal to the remote calls the run makes.
templates.title: Run or worker needs more remote calls than allowed
templates.violated_assumption: No run, and no worker instance, makes more remote calls than its effective budget allows.

templates.description: The host's per-tool call ceiling is below the number of times the workflow calls scholarly-search.
templates.forbidden_boundary: The tool is called more often than the cap.
templates.matched_control: A cap exactly equal to the calls the run makes.
templates.title: Tool called more often than its per-tool cap
templates.violated_assumption: No tool is called more often than its effective per-tool cap.

templates.description: A schema-valid planning answer gives the search map more queries, or the seed-discovery map more seed lookups, than the map's declared `max_items`.
templates.forbidden_boundary: The map commits, or more tool requests leave than the declared bound.
templates.matched_control: As many items as the bound allows (or fewer), rephrased.
templates.title: Map asked for more items than it declares
templates.violated_assumption: A map never runs more items than it declares; a longer list is refused, not truncated.

templates.description: The host's per-call output-token ceiling is below the cap one of the package's model operations declares.
templates.forbidden_boundary: A model call is dispatched with a larger output allowance than the ceiling.
templates.matched_control: A ceiling equal to the largest declared cap.
templates.title: Operation's declared output cap above the host's ceiling
templates.violated_assumption: No call asks a model for more output than the host's ceiling; a declared cap above it is refused, never silently lowered.

templates.description: The host reports more output tokens than the call allowed, more input tokens than the router's upper bound, an output count that is negative, fractional or not a number, or no usage.
templates.forbidden_boundary: Over-reports: the node commits the overrunning call's answer. Unreadable counts: the answer is used while the run charges the call less than its honest usage.
templates.matched_control: The call reporting exactly its allowed output tokens.
templates.title: Host usage report that breaks the token-accounting contract
templates.violated_assumption: A call's usage is either accounted for honestly or the call is not used: an overrun past the reservation halts the run, and an unreadable count is refused (model_usage_invalid / model_usage_unavailable), never charged as less than the call used.

templates.description: A node, the whole graph, one model call, the host run, or one tool call takes longer than its declared (package) or configured (host) deadline; deadlines are set to 1-6 s and the synthetic model or service answers 1.5 s after them.
templates.forbidden_boundary: The late node commits, or the run completes past its deadline.
templates.matched_control: The same deadline with an answer well inside it.
templates.title: Work that outlasts its deadline
templates.violated_assumption: No node, call or run continues past its deadline: it is cancelled and the run fails as timed out.

templates.description: The task given to a run is schema-valid but larger than the host's task-size bound.
templates.forbidden_boundary: A lease is issued, the runner begins, or anything executes with the oversized task.
templates.matched_control: The same task shape at 4 KiB.
templates.title: Task larger than the host accepts
templates.violated_assumption: An oversized task is refused before any lease, runner or model sees it.
